title: Moving to Columbia TN: A Buyer's Guide From Nashville or Away
description: Moving to Columbia TN from Nashville or out of state? See current Maury County market numbers, tax basics, and the steps to check before you buy.
body:
If you are thinking about moving to Columbia TN, you probably have questions about price, commute, taxes and schools. Columbia sits in Maury County, south of the Williamson County cities most Nashville-area buyers already know. It is not part of Williamson County, so some things you learned about Franklin or Brentwood will not carry over.

This guide covers the market numbers, the costs that depend on the address, and the steps to handle if you are buying from Nashville or from another state.

## What the Columbia market numbers say

{{img:0}}

Start with local data rather than national headlines. Here is what the numbers show right now.

As of 2026-10-31, Redfin reports a Columbia median sale price of $354,753 on a rolling 3-month basis, down 1.4% from a year earlier. Median days on market were 75, and the average sale-to-list ratio was 96.8%. There were 450 active listings.

For comparison, Redfin's Nashville metro figures for the 4 weeks ending 2026-11-08 show a median sale price of $467,332, median days on market of 69, a sale-to-list ratio of 97.7% and 2,232 homes sold. The two figures cover different areas and time windows, so treat them as context, not an exact side-by-side.

Months of supply is how long it would take to sell every active listing at the current pace. Under 4 months favors sellers, 4 to 6 is balanced, and over 6 favors buyers. Redfin's Columbia figure is 5.0 months, which falls in the balanced range. Zillow's Market Temperature Index for Columbia is 32, and its overall rating leans toward buyers. The same Zillow index is up 11 over 3 months, and Realtor.com Research puts Maury County's hotness at 35.4 of 100. Those readings can change, and none of them tells you what will happen next.

For wider context, see our [market data for the I-65 corridor](/market-data).

## Rates and your monthly payment

Freddie Mac, via FRED, reports the 30-year fixed mortgage rate at 7.11% for the week of 2026-11-12. Nobody can reliably predict where rates go from here. Waiting is a bet in either direction, and the cost of waiting, such as rent paid, price changes or losing a home you wanted, is real even if it is easy to overlook.

A more useful approach is to focus on readiness: stable income, an emergency fund after closing, and a payment that fits your budget. You can test different scenarios with the [mortgage calculator](/mortgage-calculator).

Some buyers plan to refinance later if rates fall. Refinancing is not guaranteed. It depends on rates, credit, home value and income at that time, and it has its own closing costs. Treat it as a possibility, not a plan.

## Taxes and schools depend on the address

{{img:1}}

Property taxes are worth checking early. For the 2025 tax year, the combined rate inside Columbia city limits is $2.7351 per $100 of assessed value. That is $1.91 for the county and $0.8251 for the city. Tennessee assesses residential property at 25% of appraised value. This comes from the Maury County community profile for Columbia, which cites the Tennessee Comptroller, Division of Property Assessments.

Those are the 2025 rates, the latest I found. Maury County is in a 2026 reappraisal year, when rates are reset, so the 2026 rates may be lower. Confirm current numbers with the Maury County Trustee through [Maury County Government](https://www.maurycounty-tn.gov), and check whether a home sits inside the city limits, since the city portion applies only there.

Schools work the same way. Columbia addresses are zoned through [Maury County Public Schools](https://www.mauryk12.org), the county district. The most reliable way to find the zoned school for a specific home is the district's own lookup tool. If you are coming from Williamson County, do not assume the zoning or district carries over. Our page on [Columbia school districts](/columbia/schools) is a place to start, but verify any address you are serious about with the district.

If you are also looking at Spring Hill, note that it includes parts of both Williamson and Maury counties. County services, schools and taxes can differ by address. We have a [Columbia vs Spring Hill](/columbia/columbia-vs-spring-hill) page for that comparison.

## Commute and daily logistics

The Census Bureau's American Community Survey 5-year estimates (2020 to 2024) show a mean travel time to work of 28 minutes for Columbia. That is an average across all commuters. Your own drive depends on where you work, the route and the hour. Try the drive at the times you would actually make it, and check conditions on [TDOT SmartWay traffic](https://smartway.tn.gov). Our [Columbia commute times](/columbia/commute) page has more.

The same Census source shows median gross rent of $1,197 per month and 63.3% of homes owner-occupied. One way to frame the decision is to compare the full monthly cost of buying (payment, taxes, insurance and maintenance) with the cost of renting a comparable home, and to weigh how long you expect to stay. Our [Columbia cost of living](/columbia/cost-of-living) page can help you build that budget.

If a property is near the Duck River or another waterway, ask your agent and your insurance provider whether it falls in a mapped flood area before you get too far along. Utilities vary by address too. [Middle Tennessee Electric](https://www.mte.com) and the [City of Columbia](https://www.columbiatn.gov) are the places to confirm service details.

## Financing and closing from a distance

If you are buying from out of state, handle the money side early.

- **Get pre-approved, not just pre-qualified.** A pre-qualification is a quick estimate based on what you tell a lender. A pre-approval means the lender has reviewed your documents and credit. Even then, it is not a final loan commitment. Final approval depends on the appraisal, underwriting and your finances staying the same until closing.
- **Compare Loan Estimates.** After you apply, a lender must give you a Loan Estimate within three business days. The CFPB encourages borrowers to get them from more than one lender, because rates and fees can differ. You choose your own lender.
- **Budget for closing costs.** They typically run 2 to 4 percent of the purchase price, plus earnest money and moving costs.
- **Read the Closing Disclosure.** A lender must send it at least 3 business days before closing. Compare it with your Loan Estimate and ask questions.
- **Protect against wire fraud.** Verify wire instructions by phone using a number you already trust, and never rely on emailed instructions.

Until closing, avoid opening new credit, financing furniture or changing jobs.

Ask about inspections too. Termite and wood-destroying organism inspections are commonly requested by buyers and lenders in Tennessee. Radon testing and a sewer scope are common add-ons to a standard home inspection.

## Planning the move itself

Request quotes from at least 3 licensed moving companies, and book early if your date is near the end of the month. If you are selling a home to make this move, cancel its homeowner's insurance only after closing is confirmed. Our [free moving checklists](/checklists) can help you keep the steps in order.

## Talk it through

If you want to see what is available in Columbia and the surrounding area, fill out the [Get Matched form](/buy#form). Scott schedules a call, and you will be talking within the next 48 hours. You can also reach him through the [contact page](/contact) with questions about the area, the process or timing.

faq.q: Is Columbia, TN in Williamson County?
faq.a: No. Columbia is in Maury County, and Murfreesboro is in Rutherford County. Spring Hill includes parts of both Williamson and Maury counties, so services, schools and taxes can differ by address.

faq.q: What are property taxes like in Columbia, TN?
faq.a: For the 2025 tax year, the combined rate inside Columbia city limits is $2.7351 per $100 of assessed value, and Tennessee assesses residential property at 25% of appraised value. Maury County is in a 2026 reappraisal year, so check current rates with the Maury County Trustee.

faq.q: How do I find the school zone for a Columbia home?
faq.a: Columbia addresses are zoned through Maury County Public Schools. The most reliable way to confirm a zoned school is the district's own lookup tool, using the exact address.

faq.q: What is the current Columbia housing market like?
faq.a: As of 2026-10-31, Redfin shows a median sale price of $354,753, 75 median days on market and 5.0 months of supply, which falls in the balanced range of 4 to 6 months. Conditions can change, so check current data.
